scope: Independent editorial review of 12 author-supplied fictional cards, 120 triples, against the ten supplied questions. Checked both orders of the two supporting details. All original IDs, anchors, item names and three-slot structures retained.
blinding: Read the three author files and the supplied question and editorial instructions. No patient text, numerical reference values, model or experiment outputs, or repository contents were seen. No generation or scoring experiment was run.

notable_revisions.GK01: Separated the bowling actors and kept compost details distinct.
notable_revisions.GK02: Replaced a recital phone alarm with an early dinner-party arrival.
notable_revisions.GK03: Kept the bike ride, kite and family farewell; clarified who acted.
notable_revisions.GK04: Replaced a charity-walk finish with a handmade serving bowl.

notable_revisions.GK06: Used ducklings, snowbound steps, a civic proposal, and a forgotten guest name.
notable_revisions.GK07: Used a team reunion, school demolition, a cave light failing, the wrong dance class, and feeding sparrows.

limits: Passage topics, sensory detail, emotional intensity, familiarity and relationship to the fixed work or hobby anchor can vary across cards. Equivalence was not tested.
Swapping supporting notes preserves their facts. Sequence can still affect emphasis, pronoun choice or response planning, especially for road steps and time-ordered incidents.

The two frames for directions and differences in meal context broaden possible accounts. They do not remove genre or wording cues. All destinations and addresses are fictional route cues, not maps that were independently verified.
